newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers swing up, volatility disturbs buyers.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers swing up, volatility disturbs buyers.

text.p: ARA bunkers swung higher on Wednesday after sharp losses on Tuesday, but Mediterranean suppliers responded to yesterday's weakness and posted their prices down, dealers said.
The confusion over fluctuating prices left ship owners uninterested in replenishing their tanks.
"I am finding it difficult to explain why (prices) all went up today, or equally why they fell yesterday," one trader said.
Rotterdam 380 CST traded in the range $115/$117 fob, some $4 higher than at Tuesday's close, itself up from midsession lows.
Early enquiries totalled no more than 10,000 tonnes.
Hamburg followed Rotterdam's lead, rising some $4 to $124/$126 fob. As in the ARA markets, however, very few buyers surfaced.
Mediterranean suppliers were more affected by Tuesday's sagging market and, on average, brought their fuel oil prices down by $2 a tonne.
Durban was also about $2 a tonne weaker, at $113/$115.
Further east, Saudi Aramco, dropped its Gulf prices by $2 a tonne to $124 for fuel oil and $223 for diesel. Red Sea prices were left unchanged.
